sa: तं ह पितोवाच श्वेतकेतो वस ब्रह्मचर्यम् ।
न वै सोम्यास्मत् कुलीनो ऽननूच्य ब्रह्मबन्धुर् इव भवतीति ॥
iast: taṃ ha pitovāca śvetaketo vasa brahmacaryam ।
na vai somyāsmat kulīno ’nanūcya brahmabandhur iva bhavatīti ॥
words: name of Śvetaketu as Āruṇi's son
belonging to the family of; of high or eminent descent; well-born

tr.text: Om. Once upon a time there was one Svetaketu, the grandson of Aruna. His father said to him, ‘O Svetaketu, live the life of a Brahmacharin. Dear boy, there never is anyone in our family who does not study and is only nominally a Brahmana.’

sa: स ह द्वादशवर्ष उपेत्य चतुर्विंशतिवर्षः सर्वान् वेदान् अधीत्य महामना अनूचानमानी स्तब्ध एयाय ।
iast: sa ha dvādaśavarṣa upetya caturviṃśativarṣaḥ sarvān vedān adhītya mahāmanā anūcānamānī stabdha eyāya ।
words: one so well versed in the Vedas and Vedāṅgas as to be able to repeat them

tr.text: Having gone (to the teacher’s house) when twelve years old, he came back when he was twenty-four old, having studied all the Vedas, conceited, arrogant and regarding himself as very learned. His father said to him, ‘Svetaketu, dear boy, you, I see, are conceited, arrogant, regarding yourself as very learned; did you ask for that teaching (about the Supreme Brahman) through which what is unheard becomes heard, what is unthought becomes thought of, what is unknown becomes known ?’ ‘Of what nature, revered sir, is that teaching ?’

sa: श्वेतकेतो यन् नु सोम्येदं महामना अनूचानमानी स्तब्धो ऽसि ।
उत तम् आदेशम् अप्राक्ष्यः येनाश्रुतं श्रुतं भवत्य् अमतं मतम् अविज्ञातं विज्ञातम् इति ।
कथं नु भगवः स आदेशो भवतीति ॥
iast: śvetaketo yan nu somyedaṃ mahāmanā anūcānamānī stabdho ’si ।
uta tam ādeśam aprākṣyaḥ yenāśrutaṃ śrutaṃ bhavaty amataṃ matam avijñātaṃ vijñātam iti ।
kathaṃ nu bhagavaḥ sa ādeśo bhavatīti ॥
words: one so well versed in the Vedas and Vedāṅgas as to be able to repeat them

tr.text: Having gone (to the teacher’s house) when twelve years old, he came back when he was twenty-four old, having studied all the Vedas, conceited, arrogant and regarding himself as very learned. His father said to him, ‘Svetaketu, dear boy, you, I see, are conceited, arrogant, regarding yourself as very learned; did you ask for that teaching (about the Supreme Brahman) through which what is unheard becomes heard, what is unthought becomes thought of, what is unknown becomes known ?’ ‘Of what nature, revered sir, is that teaching ?’

sa: यथा सोम्यैकेन मृत्पिण्डेन सर्वं मृन्मयं विज्ञातं स्यात् ।
वाचारम्भणं विकारो नामधेयं मृत्तिकेत्य् एव सत्यम् ॥
iast: yathā somyaikena mṛtpiṇḍena sarvaṃ mṛnmayaṃ vijñātaṃ syāt ।
vācārambhaṇaṃ vikāro nāmadheyaṃ mṛttikety eva satyam ॥
words: any round or roundish mass or heap; a ball; globe
speech; a word; the goddess of speech
the act of taking hold of; seizing; using
change of form or nature; alteration or deviation from any natural state; transformation

tr.text: ‘Dear boy, just as through a single clod of clay all that is made of clay would become known, for all modifications is but name based upon words and the clay alone is real;

sa: यथा सोम्यैकेन लोहमणिना सर्वं लोहमयं विज्ञातं स्यात् ।
वाचारम्भणं विकारो नामधेयं लोहम् इत्य् एव सत्यम् ॥
iast: yathā somyaikena lohamaṇinā sarvaṃ lohamayaṃ vijñātaṃ syāt ।
vācārambhaṇaṃ vikāro nāmadheyaṃ loham ity eva satyam ॥
words: speech; a word; the goddess of speech
the act of taking hold of; seizing; using
change of form or nature; alteration or deviation from any natural state; transformation

tr.text: Dear boy, just as through a single ingot of gold, all that is made of gold would become known, for all modification is but name based upon words and the gold alone is real;

sa: यथा सोम्यैकेन नखनिकृन्तनेन सर्वं कार्ष्णायसं विज्ञातं स्यात् ।
वाचारम्भणं विकारो नामधेयं कृष्णायसम् इत्य् एव सत्यम् ।
iast: yathā somyaikena nakhanikṛntanena sarvaṃ kārṣṇāyasaṃ vijñātaṃ syāt ।
vācārambhaṇaṃ vikāro nāmadheyaṃ kṛṣṇāyasam ity eva satyam ।
words: speech; a word; the goddess of speech
the act of taking hold of; seizing; using
change of form or nature; alteration or deviation from any natural state; transformation

tr.text: Dear boy, just as through a single nail-parer all that is made of iron would become known, for all modification is but name based upon words and the iron alone is real – such, dear boy, is that teaching.’

sa: न वै नूनं भगवन्तस् त एतद् अवेदिषुः ।
यद् ध्य् एतद् अवेदिष्यन् कथं मे नावक्ष्यन् ।
इति भगवांस् त्व् एव मे ब्रवीत्व् इति ।
iast: na vai nūnaṃ bhagavantas ta etad avediṣuḥ ।
yad dhy etad avediṣyan kathaṃ me nāvakṣyan ।
iti bhagavāṃs tv eva me bravītv iti ।

tr.text: ‘Surely, my revered teachers did not know it, for if they had known, why should they not have told it to me ? However, revered father, teach it to me’. ‘Be it so, dear boy’, said (the father).

sa: सद् एव सोम्येदम् अग्र आसीद् एकम् एवाद्वितीयम् ।
तद् धैक आहुर् असद् एवेदम् अग्र आसीद् एकम् एवाद्वितीयम् ।
iast: sad eva somyedam agra āsīd ekam evādvitīyam ।
tad dhaika āhur asad evedam agra āsīd ekam evādvitīyam ।

tr.text: ‘In the beginning, dear boy, this was Being alone, one only, without a second. Some say that, in the beginning, this was Non-being alone, one only, without a second. From that Non-being arose Being.’

sa: कुतस् तु खलु सोम्यैवं स्याद् इति होवाच ।
सत् त्व् एव सोम्येदम् अग्र आसीद् एकम् एवाद्वितीयम् ॥
iast: kutas tu khalu somyaivaṃ syād iti hovāca ।
sat tv eva somyedam agra āsīd ekam evādvitīyam ॥

tr.text: Aruni said, ‘But now, indeed, dear boy, could it be so ? How could Being arise from Non-being ? In truth, dear boy, in the beginning (before creation), there was Being alone, one only, without a second.

sa: तस्माद् यत्र क्व च शोचति स्वेदते वा पुरुषस् तेजस एव तद् अध्य् आपो जायन्ते ॥
iast: tasmād yatra kva ca śocati svedate vā puruṣas tejasa eva tad adhy āpo jāyante ॥

tr.text: ‘That Being willed, "May I become many, may I grow forth." It created fire. That fire willed, "May I become many, may I grow forth". It created water. Therefore whenever a man grieves or perspires, then it is from fire that water issues.

sa: ता आप ऐक्षन्त बह्व्यः स्याम प्रजायेमहीति ता
अन्नमसृजन्त तस्माद्यत्र क्व च वर्षति तदेव भूयिष्ठमन्नं
iast: tā āpa aikṣanta bahvyaḥ syāma prajāyemahīti tā
annamasṛjanta tasmādyatra kva ca varṣati tadeva bhūyiṣṭhamannaṃ

tr.text: ‘That water willed, "May I become many, may I grow forth." It created food. Therefore wherever it rains, abundant food grows there; it is from water that food for eating is produced.

sa: तेषां खल्व् एषां भूतानां त्रीण्य् एव बीजानि भवन्त्य् आण्डजं जीवजम् उद्भिज्जम् इति ॥
iast: teṣāṃ khalv eṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ trīṇy eva bījāni bhavanty āṇḍajaṃ jīvajam udbhijjam iti ॥

tr.text: ‘Of the aforesaid beings there are only three origins: those born from eggs, born from living beings, and born from sprouts.

sa: हन्ताहम् इमास् तिस्रो देवता अनेन जीवेनात्मनानुप्रविश्य नामरूपे व्याकरवाणीति ॥
iast: hantāham imās tisro devatā anena jīvenātmanānupraviśya nāmarūpe vyākaravāṇīti ॥

tr.text: ‘That deity willed, ‘Well, let me, entering into these three deities through this living self (Jivatman), differentiate name and form.

sa: सेयं देवतेमास् तिस्रो देवता अनेनैव जीवेनात्मनानुप्रविश्य नामरूपे व्याकरोत् ॥
iast: seyaṃ devatemās tisro devatā anenaiva jīvenātmanānupraviśya nāmarūpe vyākarot ॥

tr.text: "Of these, let me make each one triplicated", willing thus, this deity entered into these three deities through this living self and differentiated names and forms.

sa: यथा तु खलु सोम्येमास् तिस्रो देवतास् त्रिवृत् त्रिवृद् एकैका भवति तन् मे विजानीहीति ॥
iast: yathā tu khalu somyemās tisro devatās trivṛt trivṛd ekaikā bhavati tan me vijānīhīti ॥

tr.text: ‘It made each one of them threefold. But, dear boy, how each of these three deities becomes threefold (outside the body), know that from me.

sa: यद् अग्ने रोहितं रूपं तेजसस् तद् रूपम् ।
वाचारम्भणं विकारो नामधेयं त्रीणि रूपाणीत्य् एव सत्यम् ॥
iast: yad agne rohitaṃ rūpaṃ tejasas tad rūpam ।
vācārambhaṇaṃ vikāro nāmadheyaṃ trīṇi rūpāṇīty eva satyam ॥
words: any outward appearance or phenomenon or colour (often pl.)
the sharp edge (of a knife etc.)
any outward appearance or phenomenon or colour (often pl.)

tr.text: ‘In fire, the red colour is the colour of fire; that which is white belongs to water and that which is black belongs to food (earth). Thus vanishes (the idea of) the quality of fire from fire; for all modification is but name based upon words, only the three forms are real.

sa: यद् आदित्यस्य रोहितं रूपं तेजसस् तद् रूपम् ।
वाचारम्भणं विकारो नामधेयं त्रीणि रूपाणीत्य् एव सत्यम् ॥
iast: yad ādityasya rohitaṃ rūpaṃ tejasas tad rūpam ।
vācārambhaṇaṃ vikāro nāmadheyaṃ trīṇi rūpāṇīty eva satyam ॥
words: name of seven deities of the heavenly sphere
any outward appearance or phenomenon or colour (often pl.)
the sharp edge (of a knife etc.)
any outward appearance or phenomenon or colour (often pl.)

tr.text: ‘In the sun, the red colour is the colour of fire, that which is white belongs to water and that which is black belongs to earth. Thus vanishes (the idea of) the quality of the sun from the sun; for all modification is but name based upon words, only the three forms are real.

sa: यच् चन्द्रमसो रोहितं रूपं तेजसस् तद् रूपम् ।
वाचारम्भणं विकारो नामधेयं त्रीणि रूपाणीत्य् एव सत्यम् ॥
iast: yac candramaso rohitaṃ rūpaṃ tejasas tad rūpam ।
vācārambhaṇaṃ vikāro nāmadheyaṃ trīṇi rūpāṇīty eva satyam ॥
words: any outward appearance or phenomenon or colour (often pl.)
the sharp edge (of a knife etc.)
any outward appearance or phenomenon or colour (often pl.)

tr.text: ‘In the moon, the red colour is the colour of fire, that which is white belongs to water and that which is black belongs to earth. Thus vanishes (the idea of) the quality of the moon from the moon; for all modification is but name based upon words, only the three forms are real.

sa: यद् विद्युतो रोहितं रूपं तेजसस् तद् रूपम् ।
वाचारम्भणं विकारो नामधेयं त्रीणि रूपाणीत्य् एव सत्यम् ॥
iast: yad vidyuto rohitaṃ rūpaṃ tejasas tad rūpam ।
vācārambhaṇaṃ vikāro nāmadheyaṃ trīṇi rūpāṇīty eva satyam ॥
words: a flashing thunderbolt (as the weapon of the Maruts)
any outward appearance or phenomenon or colour (often pl.)
the sharp edge (of a knife etc.)
any outward appearance or phenomenon or colour (often pl.)

tr.text: ‘In lightning, the red colour is the colour of fire, that which is white belongs to water and that which is black belongs to earth. Thus vanishes (the idea of) the quality of lightning from lightning; for all modification is but name based upon words, only the three forms are real.

sa: एतद् ध स्म वै तद्विद्वांस आहुः पूर्वे महाशाला महाश्रोत्रियाः ।
न नो ऽद्य कश्चनाश्रुतम् अमतम् अविज्ञातम् उदाहरिष्यति ।
iast: etad dha sma vai tadvidvāṃsa āhuḥ pūrve mahāśālā mahāśrotriyāḥ ।
na no ’dya kaścanāśrutam amatam avijñātam udāhariṣyati ।
words: being before or in front fore
a Brāhman versed in the Veda

tr.text: ‘It was indeed on knowing this (triplication) that the ancient great householders and great Vedic scholars said, ‘There is, at present, nothing that anyone would point out to us as unheard, unthought or unknown"; for from these they understood everything.

sa: यद् उ रोहितम् इवाभूद् इति तेजसस् तद् रूपम् इति तद् विदां चक्रुः ।
यद् उ शुक्लम् इवाभूद् इत्य् अपां रूपम् इति तद् विदां चक्रुः ।
यद् उ कृष्णम् इवाभूद् इत्य् अन्नस्य रूपम् इति तद् विदां चक्रुः ॥
iast: yad u rohitam ivābhūd iti tejasas tad rūpam iti tad vidāṃ cakruḥ ।
yad u śuklam ivābhūd ity apāṃ rūpam iti tad vidāṃ cakruḥ ।
yad u kṛṣṇam ivābhūd ity annasya rūpam iti tad vidāṃ cakruḥ ॥
words: the sharp edge (of a knife etc.)
any outward appearance or phenomenon or colour (often pl.)
any outward appearance or phenomenon or colour (often pl.)
any outward appearance or phenomenon or colour (often pl.)

tr.text: ‘Whatever else appeared red, that also they knew to be the colour of (untriplicated) fire; whatever appeared white, that also they knew to be the colour of water; whatever appeared black, that also they knew to be the colour of earth.

sa: यद् व् अविज्ञातम् इवाभूद् इत्य् एतासाम् एव देवतानां समास इति तद् विदां चक्रुः ।
यथा नु खलु सोम्येमास् तिस्रो देवताः पुरुषं प्राप्य त्रिवृत् त्रिवृद् एकैका भवति तन् मे विजानीहीति ॥
iast: yad v avijñātam ivābhūd ity etāsām eva devatānāṃ samāsa iti tad vidāṃ cakruḥ ।
yathā nu khalu somyemās tisro devatāḥ puruṣaṃ prāpya trivṛt trivṛd ekaikā bhavati tan me vijānīhīti ॥

tr.text: ‘Whatever appeared to be unknown, that also they knew to be a combination of these very deities. But, dear boy, know from me how, on reaching man, each of these three deities becomes threefold.

sa: तस्य यः स्थविष्ठो धातुस् तत् पुरीषं भवति ।
iast: tasya yaḥ sthaviṣṭho dhātus tat purīṣaṃ bhavati ।
words: (superl. of sthūra) very broad or thick or solid or strong

tr.text: ‘Food, when eaten, becomes divided into three parts. What is its grossest ingredient, that becomes faeces; what is the middling ingredient, that becomes flesh; and what is the subtlest ingredient, that becomes mind.

sa: तासां यः स्थविष्ठो धातुस् तन् मूत्रं भवति ।
iast: tāsāṃ yaḥ sthaviṣṭho dhātus tan mūtraṃ bhavati ।
words: (superl. of sthūra) very broad or thick or solid or strong
the fluid secreted by the kidneys

tr.text: ‘Water, when drunk, becomes divided into three parts. What is its grossest ingredient, that becomes urine; what is the middling ingredient, that becomes blood; and what is the subtlest ingredient, that becomes Prana.

sa: तस्य यः स्थविष्ठो धातुस् तद् अस्थि भवति ।
iast: tasya yaḥ sthaviṣṭho dhātus tad asthi bhavati ।
words: the sharp edge (of a knife etc.)
(superl. of sthūra) very broad or thick or solid or strong

tr.text: ‘Fire, when eaten, becomes divided into three parts. What is its grossest ingredient, that becomes bone; what is the middling ingredient, that becomes marrow; and what is the subtlest ingredient, hat becomes speech.

sa: भूय एव मा भगवान् विज्ञापयत्व् इति ।
iast: bhūya eva mā bhagavān vijñāpayatv iti ।

tr.text: ‘Hence, dear boy, mind is made up of food, Prana is made up of water, and speech is made of fire. ‘Explain it further to me, revered sir’. ‘Be it so, dear boy’, said the father.

sa: दध्नः सोम्य मथ्यमानस्य यो ऽणिमा स ऊर्ध्वः समुदीषति ।
iast: dadhnaḥ somya mathyamānasya yo ’ṇimā sa ūrdhvaḥ samudīṣati ।

tr.text: ‘Dear boy, of the curd that is being churned that which is the subtlest part rises upwards and that becomes butter.

sa: एवम् एव खलु सोम्यान्नस्याश्यमानस्य यो ऽणिमा स ऊर्ध्वः समुदीषति ।
iast: evam eva khalu somyānnasyāśyamānasya yo ’ṇimā sa ūrdhvaḥ samudīṣati ।

tr.text: ‘So also, dear boy, of the food that is eaten that which is the subtlest part rises upwards and that becomes the mind.

sa: अपां सोम्य पीयमानानां यो ऽणिमा स ऊर्ध्वः समुदीषति ।
iast: apāṃ somya pīyamānānāṃ yo ’ṇimā sa ūrdhvaḥ samudīṣati ।

tr.text: ‘Dear boy, of the water that is drunk that which is the subtlest part rises upwards and that becomes Prana.

sa: तेजसः सोम्याश्यमानस्य यो ऽणिमा स ऊर्ध्वः समुदीषति ।
iast: tejasaḥ somyāśyamānasya yo ’ṇimā sa ūrdhvaḥ samudīṣati ।
words: the sharp edge (of a knife etc.)

tr.text: ‘Dear boy, of the fire that is eaten that which is the subtlest part rises upwards and that becomes speech.

sa: भूय एव मा भगवान् विज्ञापयत्व् इति ।
iast: bhūya eva mā bhagavān vijñāpayatv iti ।

tr.text: ‘Hence, dear boy, mind is made up of food, Prana is made up of water, and speech is made up of fire’. ‘Explain it further to me, revered sir’. ‘Be it so, dear boy’, said the father.

sa: आपोमयः प्राणो न पिबतो विच्छेत्स्यत इति ॥
iast: āpomayaḥ prāṇo na pibato vicchetsyata iti ॥
words: to cut or tear or cleave or break asunder

tr.text: ‘Dear boy, man consists of sixteen parts. Do not eat for fifteen days; drink as much water as you like. Prana is made up of water, and the Prana of one who drinks water is not cut off.

sa: अथ हैनम् उपससाद किं ब्रवीमि भो इति ।
स होवाच न वै मा प्रतिभान्ति भो इति ॥
iast: atha hainam upasasāda kiṃ bravīmi bho iti ।
sa hovāca na vai mā pratibhānti bho iti ॥
words: a metrical hymn or song of praise

tr.text: Svetaketu did not eat for fifteen days. Then he approached him saying, ‘What shall I say ?’ The father said, ‘The Riks, the Yajus, and the Samans, dear boy.’ ‘They do not at all arise in me, sir’.

sa: तं होवाच यथा सोम्य महतो ऽभ्याहितस्यैको ऽङ्गारः खद्योतमात्रः परिशिष्टः स्यात् ।
तेन ततो ऽपि न बहु दहेत् ।
एवं सोम्य ते षोडशानां कलानाम् एका कला अतिशिष्टा स्यात् ।
iast: taṃ hovāca yathā somya mahato ’bhyāhitasyaiko ’ṅgāraḥ khadyotamātraḥ pariśiṣṭaḥ syāt ।
evaṃ somya te ṣoḍaśānāṃ kalānām ekā kalā atiśiṣṭā syāt ।

tr.text: The father said to him, ‘Dear boy, just as a single ember of the size of a firefly, left over from a large burning fire, cannot burn any more than that, even so, dear boy, of your sixteen parts only one part is left over, now by means of that you cannot perceive the Vedas. Eat, then you will understand me’.

tr.text: He ate and then approached his father. Whatever he asked him, he answered them all.

tr.text: The father said to him, ‘Dear boy, just as when a single ember of the size of a firefly left over from a large burning fire, is made to blaze up by adding straw and it burns much more than before, even so, dear boy, of your sixteen parts, only one part remained, and that being nourished by food, has been made to blaze up; and by that you perceive the Vedas now. Hence, dear boy, the mind is made up of food, the Prana is made up of water, and speech is made up of fire. From his words, (Svetaketu) understood it – yea, he understood it.

tr.text: Once Uddalaka Aruni said to his son Svetaketu, ‘Dear boy, know from me the true nature of sleep. When a man is said to be sleeping, then, dear boy, he has become united with Being and has attained his own nature. Hence people speak of him as sleeping, for them he has attained his own nature.

tr.text: ‘Just as a bird tied to a string, after flying in various directions and finding no resting place elsewhere, takes refuge at the very place where to it is tied, even so, dear boy, that mind, after flying in various directions and finding no resting place elsewhere, takes refuge in Prana alone; for the mind, dear boy, is tied to Prana.

sa: यत्रैतत् पुरुषो ऽशिशिषति नामाप एव तद् अशितं नयन्ते ।

tr.text: ‘Dear boy, know from me (the true nature of) hunger and thirst. When a man is said to be hungry, then (it is to be understood that), water is leading away what has been eaten; (therefore water may be designated as hunger). Just as people speak of the leader of cows, the leader of horses, and the leader of men, even so they speak of water as the leader of food. Hence, dear boy, know this shoot (the body) to be put forth (by a root), for it cannot be without a root.

sa: एवम् एव खलु सोम्यान्नेन शुङ्गेनापो मूलम् अन्विच्छ ।
अद्भिः सोम्य शुङ्गेन तेजो मूलम् अन्विच्छ ।

All these creatures, dear boy, have Being as their root, have Being as their abode, and have Being as their support.

ता यथा तत्र न विदुर् इयम् अहम् अस्मीयम् अहम् अस्मीति ॥

tr.text: ‘These eastern rivers, dear boy, flow along to the east and the western ones to the west. They rise from the ocean and merge in the ocean, and become that ocean itself. And there as these rivers do not know themselves as "I am this river, I am that river", even so, dear boy, all these creatures, having come from Being, do not know, "We have come from Being". And whatever these creatures were here, tiger or lion or wolf or boar or worm or flying insect or gad-fly or mosquito, that they become again.

tr.text: ‘Of this large tree, dear boy, if anyone were to strike at the root, it would exude sap, though still living; if anyone were to strike in the middle, it would exude sap, though still living; if anyone were to strike at the top, it would exude sap, though still living. As that tree is pervaded by the living self, it stands firm, drinking constantly and rejoicing.

sa: अस्य यद् एकां शाखां जीवो जहात्य् अथ सा शुष्यति ।

tr.text: The father said, ‘Dear boy, know that even so, being left by the living self this body surely dies, but the living self does not die. That Being which is this subtle essence (cause), even That all this world has for its self. That is the true. That is the Atman. That thou art, O Svetaketu.’ ‘Revered sir, please explain it further to me’. ‘So be it, dear boy’, said (the father).

‘Bring a fruit from this Banyan tree’. ‘Here it is, revered sir’. ‘Break it.’ ‘It is broken, revered sir’. ‘What do you see in this ?’ ‘These seeds, small like particles, revered sir’. ‘Break one of these, my child’. ‘It is broken, revered sir’. ‘What do you see in it ?’ ‘Nothing, revered sir’.

tr.text: The father said to him, ‘Dear boy, this subtle essence which you do not perceive, growing from this subtle essence the large Banyan tree thus stands. Have faith, dear boy.’

tr.text: ‘Put this salt into water and then come to me in the morning’. He did so. The father said to him, ‘Bring the salt, my child, which you put into water at night’. Having searched for it, he did not find it, as it has completely dissolved. ‘My child, take a sip from the top of this water. How is it?’ ‘It is salt’. ‘Take a sip from the middle. How is it ?’ ‘It is salt’. ‘Take a sip from the bottom. How is it ?’ ‘It is salt’. ‘Throw this water away and then come to me’. He did so (and returned saying), ‘It is there always’. The father said to him, ‘Dear boy, as you do not see what is present in this water though indeed it exists in it, similarly, (Being exists) indeed in this body.

(a particle of asseveration or emphasis) indeed

tr.text: ‘Put this salt into water and then come to me in the morning’. He did so. The father said to him, ‘Bring the salt, my child, which you put into water at night’. Having searched for it, he did not find it, as it has completely dissolved. ‘My child, take a sip from the top of this water. How is it?’ ‘It is salt’. ‘Take a sip from the middle. How is it ?’ ‘It is salt’. ‘Take a sip from the bottom. How is it ?’ ‘It is salt’. ‘Throw this water away and then come to me’. He did so (and returned saying), ‘It is there always’. The father said to him, ‘Dear boy, as you do not see what is present in this water though indeed it exists in it, similarly, (Being exists) indeed in this body.

takeaway: Like salt dissolved in water, the Real is invisible but present in every drop.

sa: स य एषो ऽणिमैतद् आत्म्यम् इदं सर्वम् ।
भूय एव मा भगवान् विज्ञापयत्व् इति ।
iast: sa ya eṣo ’ṇimaitad ātmyam idaṃ sarvam ।
bhūya eva mā bhagavān vijñāpayatv iti ।

tr.text: ‘That Being which is this subtle essence (cause), even That all this world has for its self. That is the true. That is the Atman. That thou art, O Svetaketu.’ ‘Revered sir, please explain it further to me’. ‘So be it, dear boy’, said (the father).

sa: यथा सोम्य पुरुषं गन्धारेभ्यो ऽभिनद्धाक्षम् आनीय तं ततो ऽतिजने विसृजेत् ।
स यथा तत्र प्राङ् वोदङ् वा अधराङ् वा प्रत्यङ् वा प्रध्मायीताभिनद्धाक्ष आनीतो ऽभिनद्धाक्षो विसृष्टः ॥
iast: yathā somya puruṣaṃ gandhārebhyo ’bhinaddhākṣam ānīya taṃ tato ’tijane visṛjet ।
sa yathā tatra prāṅ vodaṅ vā adharāṅ vā pratyaṅ vā pradhmāyītābhinaddhākṣa ānīto ’bhinaddhākṣo visṛṣṭaḥ ॥

tr.text: ‘Just as, dear boy, (some robber) having brought a man from the Gandhara region with his eyes bound up, might leave him in a very desolate place, and just as that man would shout towards the east, or towards the north, or towards the south, or towards the west, (saying) "I have been brought here with my eyes bound up, I have been left here with my eyes bound up."’

sa: तस्य यथाभिनहनं प्रमुच्य प्रब्रूयाद् एतां दिशं गन्धारा एतां दिशं व्रजेति ।
स ग्रामाद् ग्रामं पृच्छन् पण्डितो मेधावी गन्धारान् एवोपसंपद्येत ।
तस्य तावद् एव चिरं यावन् न विमोक्ष्ये ऽथ संपत्स्य इति ॥
iast: tasya yathābhinahanaṃ pramucya prabrūyād etāṃ diśaṃ gandhārā etāṃ diśaṃ vrajeti ।
sa grāmād grāmaṃ pṛcchan paṇḍito medhāvī gandhārān evopasaṃpadyeta ।
tasya tāvad eva ciraṃ yāvan na vimokṣye ’tha saṃpatsya iti ॥

tr.text: ‘And as some one might remove his bandage and tell him, "The Gandhara region is in this direction, proceed in this direction" and as he, enquiring his way from village, to village and being instructed and capable of judging by himself would reach the Gandhara region itself, even so, in this world that person knows who has a preceptor. And for him, only so long is the delay as he is not liberated (from the body) and then immediately he is merged in Being.

sa: स य एषो ऽणिमैतद् आत्म्यम् इदं सर्वम् ।
भूय एव मा भगवान् विज्ञापयत्व् इति ।
iast: sa ya eṣo ’ṇimaitad ātmyam idaṃ sarvam ।
bhūya eva mā bhagavān vijñāpayatv iti ।

tr.text: ‘That Being which is this subtle essence (cause), even That all this world has for its self. That is the true. That is the Atman. That thou art, O Svetaketu.’ ‘Revered sir, please explain it further to me’. ‘So be it, dear boy’, said (the father).

sa: पुरुषं सोम्योतोपतापिनं ज्ञातयः पर्युपासते जानासि मां जानासि माम् इति ।
तस्य यावन् न वाङ् मनसि संपद्यते मनः प्राणे प्राणस् तेजसि तेजः परस्यां देवतायां तावज् जानाति ॥
iast: puruṣaṃ somyotopatāpinaṃ jñātayaḥ paryupāsate jānāsi māṃ jānāsi mām iti ।
tasya yāvan na vāṅ manasi saṃpadyate manaḥ prāṇe prāṇas tejasi tejaḥ parasyāṃ devatāyāṃ tāvaj jānāti ॥

tr.text: ‘Dear boy, the relatives of a man who is ill assemble round him and ask, "Do you recognise me ? Do you recognise me ?" As long as his speech is not merged in the mind, the mind in Prana, Prana in fire, and fire in the supreme deity, so long does he know them.

sa: अथ यदास्य वाङ् मनसि संपद्यते मनः प्राणे प्राणस् तेजसि तेजः परस्यां देवतायाम् अथ न जानाति ॥
iast: atha yadāsya vāṅ manasi saṃpadyate manaḥ prāṇe prāṇas tejasi tejaḥ parasyāṃ devatāyām atha na jānāti ॥

tr.text: ‘Then when his speech is merged in the mind, the mind in Prana, Prana in fire, and fire in the supreme deity, then he does not know them.

sa: स य एषो ऽणिमैतद् आत्म्यम् इदं सर्वम् ।
भूय एव मा भगवान् विज्ञापयत्व् इति ।
iast: sa ya eṣo ’ṇimaitad ātmyam idaṃ sarvam ।
bhūya eva mā bhagavān vijñāpayatv iti ।

tr.text: ‘That Being which is this subtle essence (cause), even That all this world has for its self. That is the true. That is the Atman. That thou art, O Svetaketu.’ ‘Revered sir, please explain it further to me’. ‘So be it, dear boy’, said (the father).

sa: अपहार्षीत् स्तेयम् अकार्षीत् परशुम् अस्मै तपतेति ।
स यदि तस्य कर्ता भवति तत एवानृतम् आत्मानं कुरुते ।
सो ऽनृताभिसंधो ऽनृतेनात्मानम् अन्तर्धाय परशुं तप्तं प्रतिगृह्णाति ।
iast: apahārṣīt steyam akārṣīt paraśum asmai tapateti ।
sa yadi tasya kartā bhavati tata evānṛtam ātmānaṃ kurute ।

tr.text: ‘Dear boy, (The officers of the king) bring a man, holding him by the hand (while saying) "He has taken something, he has committed a theft, heat the axe for him". If he is doer of that, then he makes himself false. And being addicted to falsehood, he covers himself with falsehood and grasps the heated axe; he is burnt, and then he is punished.

sa: स सत्याभिसन्धः सत्येनात्मानम् अन्तर्धाय परशुं तप्तं प्रतिगृह्णाति ।
iast: sa satyābhisandhaḥ satyenātmānam antardhāya paraśuṃ taptaṃ pratigṛhṇāti ।

tr.text: ‘If, however, he is not the doer of that, then he makes himself true. And being attached to truth, he covers himself with truth and grasps the heated axe; he is not burnt and then he is released.

sa: तद् धास्य विजज्ञाव् इति विजज्ञाव् इति ॥
iast: tad dhāsya vijajñāv iti vijajñāv iti ॥

tr.text: ‘And as in this case he (the man attached to truth) is not burnt, (similarly a man of knowledge is not born again). Thus has all this world That for its self. That is the true. That is the Atman. That thou art, O Svetaketu.’ From his words Svetaketu understood That – yea, he understood.
